text.p: Tyremaker Michelin said its 1996 first-half activity was satisfying, as strong sales growth in Asia and Latin America more than offset weakness in European and North American markets.
"During the first half of 1996, Michelin's activity, superior to the previous year, was satisfying overall," it said in its first-half statement.

Turnover rose 5.4 percent in the first half to 34.91 billion francs. "This evolution is due primarily to two factors -- an increase in sales volumes and in prices," it said. Michelin's prices were on average two percent above year-earlier levels.

Michelin said production cost reductions accounted for around 40 percent of the improvement in its first-half operating profit, which rose to 3.62 billion francs from 2.76 billion in the first half of 1995.
